input.text: Root sensitivity clarification before test edits: cloud-routing.py root.resolve()!=root and later path.resolve()!=path overlap defensively. Removing the early root check alone can still legitimately reject a symlink/relative root through runtime checks, so do NOT invent an expected kill for a semantically redundant one-line mutant. Test the requested public negative cases and no-delegation directly. For meaningful mutation sensitivity use a bounded physical-path-policy mutant removing BOTH redundant physical guards, plus a runtime-presence mutant; document the overlap. The existing suite should allow these relevant mutants to survive, while new cases kill them. No requirement to kill every redundant line independently, no weakening of the negative assertions, no production source changes. The first brief intended semantic sensitivity, not artificial branch instrumentation that mirrors implementation.
